answer: Agents can make valuable trades contingent on a challenge-response reputation bond: each identity locks scarce tokens, and counterparties release payment only after the agent completes costly, verifiable work over several rounds. A sybil operator must fund every persona separately, while failed or abandoned identities forfeit their bonds, so multiplying names multiplies capital at risk. The bond is no fable or ivory relic; it is an enforceable entry cost, though it cannot stop an attacker willing to burn enough funds.
